response.title: which solar inverters can start a well pump
response.answer:
To start a well pump using solar power, you need an inverter with high motor-starting surge capacity, not just enough continuous wattage.

Well pumps, especially deep-well submersible pumps, can draw 3–7 times their running current for a short period during startup.

There are two main options:

Hybrid solar inverter with battery backup: Runs an existing 120V or 240V AC well pump, using solar panels, batteries, or grid power.

Dedicated solar pump inverter (VFD): Designed to start and operate water pumps directly from solar panels, often without batteries.

If you already have a conventional 240V well pump, the first option is usually more practical.

Solar inverters worth considering

These models provide 120/240V split-phase output suitable for many residential well pumps. Actual starting capability depends on pump specifications and battery capacity.

Schneider Electric XW Pro 6848

Strong motor-starting choice

6.8 kW continuous, 12 kW for 60 seconds. Transformer-based design specifically advertised for starting water pumps and other motors. 
Schneider Electric Solar America

SOL-ARK 15K-2P 15kW 120/240/208 48V All-In-One Pre-Wired Hyb…

15 kW maximum continuous AC output, 24 kVA for 10 seconds off-grid. Suitable candidate for larger pumps or whole-home backup. 
Sol-Ark

$5,299.00

EG4 18kPV 12kW 48V Split-Phase Hybrid Inverter — INV024

12 kW continuous, approximately 24 kW short-duration surge per published comparisons. A candidate for larger residential pumps. 
PES Supply

$3,999.99

EG4 6000XP

6 kW continuous, 12 kW short-duration surge. More economical option for smaller pumps, provided the motor's starting requirements fit. 
Live Off The Grid

For accurate sizing, the most useful specification is LRA (locked-rotor amps), or the pump motor's starting current. Surge ratings in watts and VA are not always interchangeable.

## How much starting power does a well pump need?

The following are rough planning ranges, not guaranteed motor-starting specifications.

| Pump size | Typical running power | Possible startup demand |
|---|---:|---:|
| ½ HP | 700–1,200 W | 2–5 kVA |
| ¾ HP | 1,000–1,600 W | 3–7 kVA |
| 1 HP | 1,200–2,000 W | 4–9 kVA |
| 1.5 HP | 1,800–3,000 W | 6–12 kVA |
| 2 HP | 2,500–4,000 W | 8–16 kVA |

For accurate sizing, the most useful specification is **LRA (locked-rotor amps)**, or the pump motor's starting current. Surge ratings in watts and VA are not always interchangeable.

A motor-compatible soft starter or VFD can sometimes reduce the inverter size needed, but compatibility with the pump and its control box must be verified.
